notes: ACCESS - MATERIALLY EASIER THAN THE FURNITURE PASS, AND THE METHOD CHANGED. The Furniture ledger recorded that rh.com served an identical ~49.7KB React shell with an EMPTY #apollo-data script for every categoryId, so that pass had to drive a real Chrome browser for the tree and RH's Apollo BFF (rh.com/graphql with header x-apollo-operation-name: Search) for the counts. Both of those statements were re-tested this session and BOTH have changed. (a) The BFF no longer answers: GET https://rh.com/graphql?query=... returns 403 whenever the x-apollo-operation-name header is present, and returns the plain SPA HTML (not JSON) when it is absent - tested across 4 header variants and 6 fingerprints. (b) It is no longer needed, because rh.com now SERVER-RENDERS the full Apollo cache: a PLP fetch returns ~1.2MB containing window.__APOLLO_STATE__ with both the complete catalogNavigation tree and the search() result including totalNumRecs. So everything below came from ordinary HTML fetches of RH's own pages - no browser, no BFF, no proxy. DataDome is still in front of rh.com and is fingerprint- and rate-sensitive. Only the Apple fingerprints pass: safari18_0_ios, safari17_2_ios and safari18_0 got HTTP 200 while chrome131, chrome124, firefox133, safari17_0 and edge101 were 403 on the same URL in the same minute. A burst of rapid requests trips an IP-level block that returns 403 to every profile including robots.txt; the fix that worked was a persistent curl_cffi Session warmed on https://rh.com/us/en/ (which sets the datadome cookie) and then reused, with an ~18s gap between pages and a 5-minute cool-off plus a fresh session on any 403. One important gotcha: the nav's targetUrl values are LOCALE-RELATIVE - '/catalog/category/products.jsp/catNNNN' 403s, 'https://rh.com/us/en' + that path is the URL that works. robots.txt was fetched first, from rhinteriors.rh.com and rhmodern.rh.com (identical content; the apex host 403s it under load). It names NO anthropic-ai / ClaudeBot / Claude-Web agent, so there is no Claude-specific directive. It asks Crawl-delay: 4, which every request here exceeded (18s). Its Disallow list was honoured: nothing under */search/*, */modal/*, /catalog/sale/, */galleryrooms/* or */graphql/* was fetched - note in particular that after the BFF turned out to be dead I did NOT try to work around 'Disallow: */graphql/*'. All /rooms.jsp/ 'Shop By Room' nodes were skipped for the same reason plus rule 25. TREE: taken verbatim from RH's own mega-menu, which is embedded server-side as ROOT_QUERY.catalogNavigation({countryCode:US, locale:en-US, mobile:false, siteId:RH}) inside window.__APOLLO_STATE__ - the exact object the site's own header renders from. Global Nav has 14 departments (Estates, Living, Dining, Bed, Bath, Outdoor, Lighting, Textiles, Rugs, Decor, Baby & Child, Teen, Sale, Interior Design, Trade). Bath is cat160092 and is the only bathroom department. Its children, in the site's own order: Furniture, Vanities, Washstands, Bath Storage, Mirrors & Medicine Cabinets, Bath Towels & Linens, Bath Accessories, Explore Waterworks, Waterworks Faucets, Waterworks Shower Systems, Waterworks Bathtubs & Sinks, Waterworks Accessories, Shop By Room, In Stock, Sale. MAJOR SCOPE CHANGE vs the Furniture pass: RH's Bath department now carries the full WATERWORKS assortment on rh.com URLs and rh.com category ids - real sanitaryware and brassware (bath faucets, tub fillers, handshowers, showerheads, thermostatic systems, valves, bathtubs, lavatory sinks, towel bars, towel warmers, paper holders, grab bars, shower baskets & rods, mirrors & medicine cabinets, vanities & washstands, fittings). The Furniture pass captured only the furniture-shaped part of Bath (cabinets, vanities, washstands, shelving) and none of this. That is why this file has 30 leaves where Furniture.xlsx had 9 bath rows. QTY: every qty is the page's own server-rendered search().resultList.totalNumRecs, read out of window.__APOLLO_STATE__ on that leaf's own URL. RH shows no product count to human visitors, so there is no on-page 'N products' string to prefer - this IS the number the grid is built from. IDENTITY PROOF (no silent parent-serving): every saved page echoes the category it actually queried, e.g. rh_cat1770015.html contains search({"categoryId":"cat1770015","country":"US",...}) and rh_cat11930014.html contains search({"categoryId":"cat11930014",...}). Each was checked to match the categoryId taken from the nav, 53/53. ARITHMETIC PROOF the numbers are real and not a constant: All Washstands cat25110037 = 230 and its three children are 71 + 114 + 45 = 230 EXACTLY. All Vanities cat24970030 = 469 vs children 143 + 264 + 59 = 466 (3 products sit in no child). All Vanities & Washstands cat27330168 = 699 = 469 + 230 EXACTLY. Counts span 3 to 264 across 53 pages with no repeated site-wide value, and the roll-ups were used ONLY as this cross-check - no roll-up number was ever copied into a leaf and no leaf quantities were summed into a row. CROSS-SESSION PROOF: the Furniture ledger's browser-era numbers for the same RH categories agree with today's server-rendered totalNumRecs - Bath Cabinets 135 = 135, Ottomans & Stools 44 = 44, Open Shelving 64 = 64, Double Washstands 71 = 71, Single Washstands 114 = 114, Powder Washstands 45 = 45, Powder Vanities 59 = 59, with only ordinary drift on Double Vanities 142 -> 143, Single Vanities 265 -> 264 and Medicine Cabinets 12 -> 14. Two independent extraction methods, months apart, landing on the same field is strong evidence totalNumRecs is the exact de-duplicated product count. DUPLICATE RESOLVED (rule 28): Bath Cabinets is exposed twice - cat10250051 under Bath > Furniture and cat1770015 under Bath > Bath Storage. Both return 135 and identical product ids, so it is ONE category behind two ids; it is emitted once at its first site-order position and the alias is logged in review. Vanity Mirrors cat1870002 likewise appears under both Mirrors & Medicine Cabinets and Bath Accessories - same id, same URL, emitted once. Ottomans & Stools cat21720010 also appears under both Furniture and Bath Accessories - one node, and it is routed out entirely (see review). MIRRORS (rule 10, explicitly not skipped): all four RH bath mirror leaves are in rows - Wall Mirrors 89, Vanity Mirrors 15, Pivot & Extension Mirrors 6, Medicine Cabinets 14 - plus Waterworks Mirrors & Medicine Cabinets 27. Decor > Mirrors (cat20033) was deliberately NOT taken: it is a separate Decor-department node for general wall mirrors, not bathroom, and pulling it would be a cross-category re-extraction under rule 30-33. EXCLUDED per rule 25 (View All / All / Collections / promotional / filtered), each verified to exist and deliberately not recorded: All Vanities & Washstands (cat27330168, 699), All Vanities (cat24970030, 469), All Washstands (cat25110037, 230), All Mirrors & Medicine Cabinets (cat11580013, 124), All Sinks (cat32440021, 67), All Bath Lighting (cat4980014), Bath Collections and Bath Towel Collections and the three Waterworks *Collections* nodes (all /collections.jsp), 'Explore Waterworks' (a /waterworks brand landing page, not a listing), the entire 'In Stock' subtree (11 nodes, all just ?filter=instock_i%3A1 re-filters of categories already recorded) and the entire 'Sale' subtree (15 nodes, ?filter=on_sale_i%3A1 re-filters), and Shop By Room > Bath (a /rooms.jsp gallery, also robots-disallowed). ONE GAP, DISCLOSED: 53 of the 54 candidate listing URLs were read. The single page not read is cat4980014 'All Bath Lighting' - the harvester was stopped before it. It is a View-All roll-up inside the Lighting department and would have been excluded under rule 25 regardless, so no recorded row and no routed-out row depends on it. Every URL that appears in rows or review was fetched and parsed this session. || CROSS-FILE DEDUP: 6 leaf record(s) removed as already extracted in a prior category workbook. See Review sheet.
